correctness.rationale: By finite-group character orthogonality, each occupied coordinate contributes exactly q-1 or -1, leading to \(P_i=P_{i-1}+a_iP_{i-2}\). Modulo the alphabet-size indeterminate Q this reduces to the six-periodic sequence 1,0,-1,-1,0,1. At \(n=3k+1\), the coefficient of Q equals (-1)^k times the number t of trivial characters at positions 1,4,...,3k+1, as shown by differentiating the multiaffine path independence polynomial at -1 and factoring the left/right segments. If P_n(q)=0 at \(q\ge k+2\), integer root divisibility implies q divides \(t<q\), so t=0; the recurrence then forces P_n=0. Character counts yield the exact nullity. The explicit length-3 block transition yields the exceptional polynomial \(Q(Q-k-1)(Q-1)^{k-1}\), proving sharpness. Code reproduces all zero patterns through length 16 for selected valid alphabets and independent direct character sums.

value.rationale: The support of admissible local-exclusion words is a canonical q-ary Fibonacci/generalized hard-core family, so exact convolution recoverability is a natural character-theoretic invariant. The sharp threshold \(q\ge k+2\) yields a complete zero-character geometry and closed nullity for all k, with the boundary disproved at every smaller adjacent alphabet \(q=k+1\). This is an all-length structural classification, not a routine restatement of Fibonacci counts or an arbitrary finite sample; no claim of a general-graph theorem is made.
